html:
English settlers landed on the empty island of Barbados in February 1627, at the place now called Holetown. The voyage was paid for by London merchants.

The island's first peoples had left or been taken by Spanish slavers long before. The settlers grew tobacco and cotton with indentured servants from England, Scotland and Ireland, along with some enslaved Africans.

Within twenty years the switch to sugar made Barbados the richest English colony. Its planters and their methods spread to Jamaica, Antigua and the Carolinas. Barbados stayed English, then British, without a break until independence in 1966 under Errol Barrow, as part of the British Empire.
